subject: goto LABEL: a `go` is emitted outside its tagbody when the same label is targeted from inside AND outside a loop
description:
MEASURED s344 (#231, docs/cpan-board14-partials-s344.md §B1). Costs Text-Balanced 07_exttag (86 rows) + 09_gentag (69 rows) on the CPAN board.

Minimal repro (perl prints F; PCL crashes):
  sub f { my $n=shift;
          if($n==0){goto failed}                        # site 1: outside a loop
          while(1){ if($n==2){goto failed} else {last} } # site 2: inside a loop
          short: return "s";                            # an INTERVENING label
          failed: return "F"; }
  print f(0), "\n";
=> Execution of a form compiled with errors. Form: (go :failed)
   Compile-time error: attempt to GO to nonexistent tag: :failed

ALL THREE ingredients are required — probed 12 neighbouring shapes, all fine:
 - drop the loop-internal goto  -> compiles (S1)
 - drop the intervening `short:` label -> compiles (R4/S4)
 - drop the loop entirely -> compiles (S4)
So the trigger is: a label targeted from BOTH inside a loop body and outside it,
with another label between the loop and the target.

LATENT, which is the dangerous part: SBCL compiles the bad form and only signals
when that branch EXECUTES. `print f(1)` on the same file is silent and correct;
only f(0) crashes. Any file with this shape is a time bomb, not a load error.

Owner area: the label/tagbody machinery (#63 dynamic goto, #124 goto into a
labeled loop, #126 watchdog forward-goto). Add a Pl/t regression with BOTH the
crashing and the neighbouring passing shapes (inverse guard).
activeForm: Fixing the two-site goto tagbody bug
